node: Marine biofouling, hull coatings, cleaning and vessel-efficiency compliance
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe for the speculative second-order node around marine biofouling, hull coatings, underwater inspection/cleaning and vessel-efficiency compliance. The best-supported US-listed reference name is PPG, which has explicit antifouling and fouling-release marine coatings tied to fuel, emissions and CII compliance. The underfollowed lane is thinner: RPM has Carboline marine coatings exposure; CODA has underwater sonar/inspection technology that could be relevant if hull inspection demand rises; Nauticus is a micro-cap speculative exception in subsea robotics/services, but hull-cleaning linkage is not yet proven. This node remains speculative until there is evidence of order acceleration, dry-dock demand, fleet adoption, regulatory pull, or shipping customers explicitly prioritizing biofouling and hull-efficiency solutions.
